Hymn.title: Hymn
Hymn.description: Represents a single hymn in the Himnario EECH Móvil application, including its unique number, title, and complete lyrics.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Hymn entity.

number.description: The unique numerical identifier of the hymn within the hymnal.

title.description: The official title of the hymn.

lyrics.description: The complete text of the hymn's lyrics.

keywords.description: Additional keywords or phrases related to the hymn's content, aiding in search functionality.

Praise.title: Praise
Praise.description: Represents a single praise song, including its title, lyrics and tone.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Praise entity (slug of the title).

title.description: The official title of the praise song.

lyrics.description: The complete text of the praise song's lyrics.

tone.description: The musical key of the praise song.

Choir.title: Choir
Choir.description: Represents a single choir song, including its title, lyrics and tone.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Choir entity (slug of the title).

title.description: The official title of the choir song.

lyrics.description: The complete text of the choir song's lyrics.

tone.description: The musical key of the choir song.

speed.description: The speed or rhythm of the song, for classification.

YouthChoir.title: YouthChoir
YouthChoir.description: Represents a single youth choir song, including its title, lyrics and tone.

id.description: Unique identifier for the YouthChoir entity (slug of the title).

title.description: The official title of the youth choir song.

lyrics.description: The complete text of the youth choir song's lyrics.

tone.description: The musical key of the youth choir song.

Repertoire.title: Repertoire
Repertoire.description: Represents a user-created repertoire or song list for a service.

SongRequest.title: SongRequest
SongRequest.description: Represents a user-submitted song pending for admin approval.

submitterName.description: The name of the person submitting the song.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores user-specific settings and preferences within the application, such as their preferred font size and favorite hymns. This entity represents the app user, assuming an external authentication system handles login details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. This ID typically originates from an external authentication system or is a unique device ID.

preferredFontSize.description: The user's preferred font size for displaying hymn lyrics. This is a UI preference.

FavoriteHymn.title: FavoriteHymn
FavoriteHymn.description: Links a specific hymn to a user's profile, indicating it has been marked as a favorite for quick access.

id.description: Unique identifier for the FavoriteHymn relationship entity.

userProfileId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who marked this hymn as a favorite. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N FavoriteHymn)

hymnId.description: Reference to the Hymn that has been marked as a favorite. (Relationship: Hymn 1:N FavoriteHymn)

addedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the hymn was added to the favorites list.

firestore.reasoning:
The Himnario EECH Móvil application's data structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable by strictly adhering to the core design principles and mandated strategies. The primary goal is to ensure Authorization Independence, debuggability, and support for QAPs (Queries as Permissions).

1.  **Hymns (`/hymns/{hymnId}`):**
    *   **Authorization Independence & QAPs:** This collection stores all public hymn data. Since all hymns are publicly accessible and read-only for all users, there are no authorization dependencies on parent documents or complex access rules. Any user can `get()` a specific hymn or `list()` all hymns, making `list` operations inherently secure without filtering, thus fulfilling the QAP mandate.
    *   **Structural Segregation:** All documents in this collection share the same security posture (public read-only), simplifying security rules to `allow read: true;`.

2.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):**
    *   **Authorization Independence:** Each `UserProfile` document is identified by the `{userId}` in the path, which directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid`. The `UserProfile` entity itself also includes an `id` field which will store the same `userId`. This denormalization ensures that authorization can be checked directly against the document's `id` field (`resource.data.id == request.auth.uid`) or the path parameter (`userId == request.auth.uid`), eliminating any need for `get()` calls to other collections for ownership verification. This makes rules atomic and easy to debug.
    *   **QAPs:** `list` operations on `/users` are not permitted; instead, users only `get()` their specific profile (`/users/{request.auth.uid}`). This ensures that unauthorized users cannot enumerate profiles, and the data remains private to the owner.
    *   **Access Modeling:** This uses the 'Private Data: Path-Based ownership' pattern, providing strong isolation for user-specific data.

3.  **Favorite Hymns (`/users/{userId}/favoriteHymns/{favoriteHymnId}`):**
    *   **Authorization Independence & QAPs:** This subcollection stores hymns favorited by a specific user. The `{userId}` in the path ensures that only the authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`) can access their own favorites. Crucially, each `FavoriteHymn` document *denormalizes* the `userProfileId` field, which matches the `userId` in the path and `request.auth.uid`. This explicit ownership within each document means that rules can verify `resource.data.userProfileId == request.auth.uid` without resorting to `get()` calls on the parent `UserProfile` document. This allows for atomic writes (e.g., adding a favorite hymn without needing to first read the user profile) and simplifies debugging.
    *   `list` operations on `/users/{userId}/favoriteHymns` are secure because the path wildcards ensure only the authenticated user can list *their own* favorites, fulfilling the QAP mandate.
    *   **Access Modeling:** This follows the 'Hierarchical Paths for User-Owned Data' pattern, extending the user's private data domain with related entities.

By implementing this structure, security rules will be concise (e.g., `allow read, write: request.auth.uid == userId;` or `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId;`), easy to understand, and highly performant as they avoid expensive `get()` calls. Structural segregation ensures homogeneous security postures within collections, further simplifying rule management.
